editorial:
Imagine starting a crime spree just because you are bored. That is exactly what happens to Michel, a guy who decides that stealing wallets is a fun little hobby. You get to follow him as he tries to get better at the game, even though he has a few friends trying to keep him on the right path. The vibe is very quiet and focused, making you feel like you are right there in the crowd with him, watching his hands move. It is not a loud action movie, but it builds a lot of tension as you wonder if he will get caught by the police inspector who is always lurking around.

What really stands out is how the movie shows the actual act of stealing. You see every tiny movement of the fingers, which makes it feel like a magic trick. The pacing is slow, which might bore some people, but it makes the moments of stress hit harder. If you like movies that focus on the small details of a crime, you will love this. You can find it for rent on Apple TV if you want a quick watch, but adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: At the end, Michel gets caught during a theft and is sent back to prison. While he is locked up, he finally has a breakdown and realizes that his life of stealing was a dead end. He meets a kind woman who helps him change his ways. The movie ends with him finding a sense of peace and hope, showing that he has finally moved past his obsession with crime to find true freedom.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves smart crime stories and old school cinema.
